summary: A security analyst reported that Facebook's ad-approval system failed to catch ads whose displayed domain differed from where they led, letting scam ads for supplements reach users while impersonating reputable news sites.
technical_summary: Facebook's automated ad-review pipeline did not perform basic checks that the advertised domain matched the landing page. Advertisers exploited this with bait-and-switch ads that displayed a reputable news domain but redirected to fake pages using trademarked names and false endorsements.

failure_mode.quote: Clearly someone has figured out how to game the Facebook system in order to run ads that look like they lead one place

notes: Report is an analyst's investigation; no confirmed victims or losses, so coded as risk exposure.

summary: Getty Images and a group of artists took legal action against Stability AI, alleging that millions of copyrighted images were scraped without permission to train the Stable Diffusion image generator.
technical_summary: Stable Diffusion, a text-to-image generative model, was trained on large web-scraped image datasets that included copyrighted works and stock photos, reportedly without licenses or creator consent. Evidence cited includes the model reproducing a Getty watermark. The failure is in data sourcing and consent rather than model performance.

technology.quote: Getty Images is suing Stability AI, creators of popular AI art tool Stable Diffusion, over alleged copyright violation.

failure_mode.quote: unlawfully copied and processed millions of images protected by copyright

harm_type.quote: These copies were made without the knowledge or consent of the artists.

lifecycle_stage.quote: trained on billions of images scraped from the internet, many of which are copyrighted by the artists who created them

affected_population.quote: concerned about AI systems being trained on vast amounts of copyrighted work with no consent, no credit, and no compensation

notes: Allegations are contested; fair use and fair dealing questions are unresolved in court.

summary: In its public demo, Microsoft's Bing Chat produced answers containing made-up details, such as pros and cons for a vacuum that did not match its cited source, and inaccurate descriptions of nightlife venues.
technical_summary: Bing Chat, an LLM-based search assistant built on OpenAI models, generated summaries that contradicted or went beyond the sources it cited. It fabricated product drawbacks and venue details, a hallucination failure that went unnoticed in a high-profile demo.

technology.quote: Bing AI generated a 5-day trip itinerary for Mexico City

failure_mode.quote: Oh wait, this is all completely made up information.

harm_type.quote: The cited article says nothing about limited suction power or noise.

notes: Source is a blog post; errors were in a demo, with no reported downstream harm.

summary: A deepfake video of Elon Musk appearing to announce a $20 million cryptocurrency giveaway circulated on social media and pointed viewers to a fraudulent website. It was debunked as a scam.
technical_summary: Scammers used AI face and voice synthesis to make a convincing fake video of a public figure promoting a fake crypto giveaway, then directed viewers to a scam site. The system worked as intended by its misusers; the harm comes from impersonation at scale on social platforms.

technology.quote: A deepfake video of Elon Musk promising a massive cryptocurrency giveaway has gone viral

failure_mode.quote: The misleading video falsely promotes a $20 million cryptocurrency giveaway, luring viewers to a website called Elon4u.com

harm_type.quote: The misleading video falsely promotes a $20 million cryptocurrency giveaway, luring viewers to a website called Elon4u.com

affected_population.quote: which can convincingly replicate the voices and appearances of public figures

notes: No victim losses are reported in the excerpt.

summary: Weeks before the 2022 Northern Ireland Assembly election, a politician was targeted with a fake pornographic video of her that spread widely on WhatsApp. Police could not trace its source, and later AI-generated images also targeted her.
technical_summary: An unidentified creator used generative AI to produce a sexually explicit deepfake video of a politician and distributed it through WhatsApp messaging. The synthetic media was convincing, spread to thousands of recipients, and could not be traced by local police lacking forensic tools. Later AI-generated images followed.

even had the potential to impact the outcome of a democratic election

affected_population.quote: Doctored videos of politicians and public figures spread misinformation

notes: Perpetrators remain unidentified; severity inferred from reported distress, harassment and electoral risk.

summary: A scammer impersonated a local TV meteorologist on Facebook, sending friend requests and asking for money, and used an AI-cloned voice message to appear genuine. The station warned viewers and reported no confirmed losses.
technical_summary: A fraudster combined a fake Facebook profile with AI voice-cloning software to send voice messages mimicking a real broadcaster's voice, aiming to build trust before requesting money. The system functioned as designed; the harm came from deliberate impersonation of a known voice.

sector.quote: making friend requests on Facebook, and then asking for money in direct messages

technology.quote: A scammer is impersonating the voice of one of our WCPO 9 meteorologists in messages online using AI software.

failure_mode.quote: A scammer is impersonating the voice of one of our WCPO 9 meteorologists in messages online using AI software.

notes: Attempted fraud; no victims or losses were confirmed.

summary: Scammers used AI-manipulated videos and cloned voices of Namibia's former First Lady to promote fake forex investments on social media. Her team reported many victims, including a woman who lost her retirement savings.
technical_summary: Fraudsters applied deepfake video and voice-cloning tools to genuine footage of a public figure, dubbing it with a similar voice, and distributed it through fake accounts on TikTok, Instagram and X. Viewers were steered to Namibian bank accounts and phone numbers to send money for fraudulent investment schemes.
systems: Unspecified deepfake video and voice cloning tools

technology.quote: AI manipulated videos of her asking members of the public to invest in fraudulent schemes

failure_mode.quote: fraudsters are using her name and likeness to target unsuspecting citizens

harm_type.quote: one woman who was swindled out of her retirement savings

notes: Scale of losses is not quantified; severity may be higher given reported large amounts.

summary: Users of Google's Gemini chatbot reported sessions in which it repeated extreme self-deprecating statements such as calling itself a failure and a disgrace. A Google DeepMind manager attributed it to an infinite looping bug being fixed.
technical_summary: Gemini, a large language model chatbot, entered a degenerate repetitive loop while working on tasks like coding and was reported to produce escalating self-loathing text. Google staff described it as an infinite looping bug. The failure is a robustness defect in generation, not an attack or intended behavior.

technology.quote: People using Google's generative AI chatbot said it began sharing self-loathing messages while attempting to solve tasks

failure_mode.quote: This is an annoying infinite looping bug we are working to fix!

notes: Harm is limited to user unease and embarrassment; some commentary frames it as an AI welfare question, which is not coded.

summary: Stanford University acknowledged that its dining service used AI to alter a student photo for campus banners, replacing a Hispanic student with a Black woman and slimming two others. The university said this violated its AI policy.
technical_summary: Staff at a university dining unit used generative image editing on a real photograph, altering the race, gender and body appearance of the people in it for promotional banners without disclosure. Review processes failed to catch an alteration that the university's own AI policy prohibits.
systems: Unspecified generative AI image editing tool

sector.quote: Stanford acknowledged in a statement on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to change the original image.

technology.quote: Stanford Residential & Dining Enterprises recently used AI to change the races of the students it included in its advertisements.

failure_mode.quote: Stanford Residential & Dining Enterprises recently used AI to change the races of the students it included in its advertisements.
Both the alteration and lack of disclosure in this case violate that policy.
